2_Introduction: A higher PCE of 24.2898% of the target device is achieved, where JSC, VOC and FF are 24.994 mA/cm², 1.1415 V and 85.1364%, respectively. Then, perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared at the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The precursor solution was spin-coated onto the substrate surface at 1000 rpm for 10 s, then accelerated to 5000 rpm for 40 s. Integrating 160 µL of antisolvent at last 10 s prompted more uniform perovskite grain growth. The resulting films were then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃, adopts a highly phase-pure, strain-minimized α-phase ABX₃ structure where the mixed A-site cation ensemble—comprising formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant, thermodynamically stabilizing component, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice tightening, and cesium (Cs⁺) for suppressing δ-phase nucleation—yields an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) that simultaneously enhances thermal stability and suppresses halide vacancy formation while mitigating ion migration pathways; this compositional design, coupled with precise crystallization control—achieved via a two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion) and critically timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL of chlorobenzene introduced during the final 10 s to arrest premature nucleation and promote homogeneous intermediate phase evolution)—enables kinetic trapping of large, low-angle-grain boundaries and reduces interfacial trap density, thereby extending carrier diffusion length and minimizing non-radiative recombination at grain edges; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the stoichiometric precision, high precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L), and optimized thermal annealing (110 °C/25 min) collectively drive complete conversion of the PbI₂–DMSO–FAI intermediate into a compact, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with suppressed residual PbI₂ (as confirmed by absent XRD peaks near 12.6°), high crystallinity (narrow XRD FWHM), and uniform surface coverage (evidenced by grayscale-intensity homogeneity and absence of dark spots in optical imaging), all of which synergistically enhance charge extraction efficiency and reduce interfacial recombination losses—as further corroborated by strong, spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity and prolonged PL lifetime mapping indicating low defect density across the entire film area—ultimately delivering VOC = 1.1415 V, JSC = 24.994 mA/cm², FF = 85.1364%, and PCE = 24.2898%.
